answer: Because the derivation is a one-way function of the marble seed, the fable timing is verifiable from the gale record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 170 keys hence pays 170 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 431 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
